nodes.label: Interface
nodes.rationale: The interface is the test surface. Callers and tests cross the same seam.

nodes.label: Depth
nodes.rationale: Depth is leverage at the interface, not a ratio of implementation lines to interface lines.

nodes.label: Seam
nodes.rationale: Michael Feathers: a place where behaviour can change without editing in that place. One adapter means a hypothetical seam; two adapters means a real one.

nodes.label: Remote but owned ports and adapters
nodes.norm_label: remote but owned ports and adapters

nodes.label: Discovery Brief
nodes.rationale: Records goal, frontend or backend or full-stack scope, affected paths, captured answers, explicit assumptions, and out-of-scope items before a plan.

nodes.label: Architecture Decision Record
nodes.rationale: A short record in docs/adr/NNNN-slug.md of a decision and why. Offer one only when the choice is hard to reverse, surprising without context, and the result of a real trade-off.

nodes.label: CONTEXT.md
nodes.rationale: A glossary of context-specific terms with tight definitions and _Avoid_ synonyms. It is not a spec and must not hold implementation decisions.

nodes.label: CONTEXT-MAP.md
nodes.rationale: Root index used when a repo has multiple bounded contexts: where each CONTEXT.md lives and how the contexts relate, including shared types and domain events.

nodes.label: API Contract
nodes.rationale: Shared method, path, auth (session cookies with withCredentials, or public /t/public/), request and response shapes, and error format. Backend owns validation; frontend mirrors it for UX.

nodes.label: Grill Me
nodes.rationale: Relentless interview to sharpen a plan or design. Model invocation is disabled; the skill delegates entirely to the grilling skill.

nodes.label: Grill With Docs
nodes.rationale: Same relentless interview as grilling, and it writes ADRs and the glossary through domain modeling as decisions crystallise.

nodes.label: Grilling
nodes.rationale: Walk each branch of the design tree one question at a time, each with a recommended answer, until dependencies between decisions are resolved. Explore the codebase when it can answer the question.

nodes.label: Handoff
nodes.rationale: Compact the conversation into a handoff document in the OS temp directory, with a suggested-skills section. Reference existing PRDs, plans, ADRs, issues, and diffs instead of duplicating them, and redact secrets and PII.

nodes.label: Deepening opportunity
nodes.rationale: A refactor that turns a shallow module into a deep one so tests and agents navigate one interface. Recommendation strength is Strong, Worth exploring, or Speculative.

nodes.label: Architecture vocabulary
nodes.rationale: Use module, interface, implementation, depth, deep, shallow, seam, adapter, leverage, and locality. Do not substitute component, service, API, signature, boundary, layer, or wrapper for those terms.

nodes.label: Architecture review HTML report
nodes.rationale: A self-contained temp HTML file using Tailwind and Mermaid from CDNs. Each candidate card has a before/after diagram, problem, solution, short wins, and an optional ADR callout. Legend: solid box is a module, dashed line is a seam, red arrow is leakage, thick dark box is a deep module.

nodes.label: Vertical slice
nodes.rationale: A thin end-to-end path through every layer the feature touches that is demoable on its own. Horizontal layer tasks such as all models or all APIs are an anti-pattern.

nodes.label: Tracer bullet
nodes.rationale: The first slice: the smallest end-to-end path that proves architecture and integration points before the scope widens.

nodes.label: HITL
nodes.rationale: Human-in-the-loop: a slice that needs a person for an architectural decision, design review, or sign-off.

nodes.label: AFK
nodes.rationale: A slice an agent can implement without human interaction. Prefer AFK over HITL when both are possible.

nodes.label: Vertical slice ordering
nodes.rationale: Order tracer bullet, then happy-path completeness, edge cases, then polish. Read path before write path. Put auth in the tracer bullet when the feature is protected. Split slices that have no single demo; merge slices with no end-to-end proof.

nodes.label: Scrape Portfolio Images
nodes.rationale: Migrate niico.com collection images locally. Launch one portfolio-scraper per collection so each agent writes only its slug folder and hover-count key.

nodes.label: Portfolio image layout
nodes.rationale: Assets land in frontend/public/imgs/nav/portfolio/{slug}/ as cover.jpg, hover/slide-N.jpg, and sub-collection files. Collections are kitchens, bath, custom-millwork, and wardrobe. Prefer -p-1080 or -p-1600 CDN variants.

nodes.label: PORTFOLIO_COLLECTION_HOVER_SLIDE_COUNTS
nodes.rationale: After download, set each collection key in frontend/consts/portfolio-nav-images.js to the count of hover/slide-*.jpg files.

nodes.label: StaffGalleryDataGrid
nodes.rationale: frontend/components/staff/gallery/StaffGalleryDataGrid.js. toolbarStart is the left slot; actions is the right slot; primary variant is the black Save button, shown only when canEdit. Already used by Hover Slides, Home Landing images, site documents, product manuals, dealers, boutique developers, blog, news, lookbooks, print publications, and sub-collection detail.

nodes.label: RED-GREEN-REFACTOR
nodes.rationale: One behavior at a time: a failing test, the minimal code that passes, then refactor only while green. Never refactor while RED, and do not write the whole suite before implementation.

nodes.label: Horizontal slice anti-pattern
nodes.rationale: Writing every test first, then all implementation, tests imagined behavior and structure. Vertical tracer bullets keep each test tied to behavior just learned.

nodes.label: Public-interface tests
nodes.rationale: Good tests are integration-style: they assert observable behavior through the public API and survive internal refactors. Bad tests mock internal collaborators, assert call order, or query storage behind the interface.

nodes.label: Mock at system boundaries
nodes.rationale: Mock external APIs, time, and sometimes the filesystem. Do not mock owned classes. Inject dependencies and prefer SDK-style operations over a generic fetcher. Backend tests use SQLite ORM round-trips; frontend Vitest mocks fetch at the network edge.

nodes.label: create_ts_component_scaffold.py
nodes.rationale: Utility that scaffolds a typed component shell from a name and an output path under the frontend components tree.

nodes.label: Phase 1 Deep Intake
nodes.rationale: Start here every time. Collect a long problem description and solution ideas, including rejected approaches, before repo exploration or design questions.

nodes.label: Working Notes
nodes.rationale: Thread-only capture of problem statement, goals, non-goals, solution ideas, codebase assertions, and open threads. Not written to disk until Phase 5.

nodes.label: Phase 2 Repo Discovery
nodes.rationale: Verify user assertions with graphify query, explain, and path before Read/Grep/Glob. Summarize verified, corrected, gaps, relevant surface, and constraints.

nodes.label: Phase 3 Design-Tree Interview
nodes.rationale: Resolve one decision branch at a time until shared understanding. Exit requires testable must-haves, explicit scope, no blocking questions, and user confirmation.

nodes.label: Decision Log
nodes.rationale: Table of ID, decision, rationale, and depends-on, maintained in working notes and copied into the PRD.

nodes.label: Phase 4 Module Sketch
nodes.rationale: Map work to concrete build/modify paths and extract pure logic from UI, HTTP, and ORM before writing the PRD. User must confirm the sketch.

nodes.label: Phase 5 Write PRD
nodes.rationale: Fill the template from working notes, discovery, decision log, and module sketch. Include current state, decision log, implementation modules, and verified assertions.

nodes.label: issues/prd-<slug>.md
nodes.rationale: Default path is issues/prd-<short-slug>.md. Revisions use -v2. Never overwrite without approval. Dated names only when the user asks.

nodes.label: Phase 6 Confirm
nodes.rationale: Report path, one-paragraph scope, deferred question count, and optional handoff to /project-manager.

nodes.label: Branch 1 Problem and Success
nodes.rationale: Root branch. Unlocks every other branch. Exit is a confirmed one-sentence problem plus measurable goals, including what is not success.

nodes.label: Branch 2 Users and Permissions
nodes.rationale: Depends on Branch 1. Exit is an agreed role-by-permission matrix. Cross-check middleware.ts, AdminAuthGuard, and DRF permissions.

nodes.label: ES Admin DS Manager Kiosk Roles
nodes.rationale: Example roles listed as public visitor, ES admin, DS manager, kiosk player, and API consumer. These names come from the older multi-product suite, not from the Care Bear Daycare brand reference.
nodes.norm_label: es admin ds manager kiosk roles

nodes.label: Branch 3 Product Surface and Scope
nodes.rationale: Depends on Branch 1. Confirms MVP, out-of-scope list, and cross-cutting concerns such as shared token, Caddy routes, and Docker rebuild.

nodes.label: IHCS Email Signatures Digital Signage
nodes.rationale: Branch 3 example products are IHCS marketing site, Email Signatures, Digital Signage, or backend-only. Care Bear Daycare is not named.

nodes.label: Branch 4 Data and Integrations
nodes.rationale: Depends on Branches 2 and 3. Covers models, lifecycle, Entra, Outlook add-in, WebSockets, migrations. Exit is an entity list and integration boundaries.

nodes.label: Branch 5 UX and Flows
nodes.rationale: Depends on Branches 2–4. Primary flow, edge cases, and design reference (Tailwind, Figma, or existing MUI). i18n probe is scoped to the IHCS website.

nodes.label: Branch 6 Non-Functional Requirements
nodes.rationale: Depends on Branches 3–5. Performance, accessibility, security, and reliability, or an explicit statement of no special requirements.

nodes.label: Branch 7 Rollout and Phasing
nodes.rationale: Depends on Branches 3–5. MVP versus later phases, feature flags, beta users, client sign-off, and launch assets.

nodes.label: Branch 8 Acceptance and Verification
nodes.rationale: Depends on all prior branches. Manual scenarios per role, API method/path/status expectations, and regression areas that prove Branch 1 success.

nodes.label: Deferred Decision
nodes.rationale: If the user is unsure, offer two or three options, record a deferral with an owner and whether it blocks MVP, and do not invent a decision.

nodes.label: Deep Module
nodes.rationale: Pure input-to-output logic with injected plain data, no UI/framework/ORM/globals/request/hooks, and a stable signature so it can be unit-tested in isolation.

nodes.label: Shallow Orchestrator
nodes.rationale: Viewsets, route pages, and hooks stay thin and delegate rules downward. Tested with integration or UI tests only.

nodes.label: Route to Orchestrator to Deep Module
nodes.rationale: Dependency shape: Route or ViewSet calls an orchestrator hook or service, which calls deep modules, with API client or serializer beside the orchestrator.
nodes.norm_label: route to orchestrator to deep module

nodes.label: Backend Frontend Cross-Cutting Layers
nodes.rationale: Sketch splits into backend models/serializers/services/viewsets, frontend pages/components/hooks/API clients, and cross-cutting middleware, auth, env, Docker, and migrations.

nodes.label: Module Table M-001
nodes.rationale: Columns: ID, module path, layer, Create/Modify/Extend, responsibility, deep flag, test approach, dependencies. Example pairs a schedule service with a thin viewset and a frontend domain preview.

nodes.label: PRD Product Field
nodes.rationale: Product placeholder lists IHCS website, Email Signatures, Digital Signage, Cross-cutting, or Other. Care Bear Daycare is not an option.

nodes.label: P0 P1 P2 Requirements
nodes.rationale: Must-have R-001, should-have R-101, and could-have R-201, each with rationale and a decision reference.

nodes.label: Requirement to Module Traceability
nodes.rationale: Maps requirement IDs to module IDs. The skill requires every P0 to map to at least one module.

nodes.label: Current State and Verified Assertions
nodes.rationale: Phase 2 section: assertion verdicts (Confirmed, Corrected, Not found), frontend/backend/other surfaces, and gaps versus the desired end state.

nodes.label: Deploy Next.js Site to Pages
nodes.rationale: On push to main or workflow_dispatch. Concurrency group pages does not cancel in progress. Build job needs deploy job. Permissions: contents read, pages write, id-token write.

nodes.label: GitHub Pages Next.js Starter Workflow
nodes.rationale: File header cites the actions/starter-workflows pages/nextjs.yml template.

nodes.label: Detect Package Manager
nodes.rationale: If frontend/yarn.lock exists, manager yarn, command install, runner yarn. Else if frontend/package.json exists, npm ci via npx. Otherwise the step fails.

nodes.label: GitHub Pages Base Path
nodes.rationale: configure-pages uses static_site_generator next and frontend/next.config.js. withPlugins() blocks the injector, so the build also sets GITHUB_PAGES and NEXT_PUBLIC_BASE_PATH from steps.pages.outputs.base_path.

nodes.label: Pages Public Env File
nodes.rationale: Build writes frontend/.env with a placeholder MUI X license, NEXT_PUBLIC_HOST https://www.niico.com, NEXT_PUBLIC_COMPANY NIICO Millwork Group LTD., and NEXT_PUBLIC_ESTABLISHED 2020.

nodes.label: NIICO Millwork Pages Identity
nodes.rationale: Deployed public env still names NIICO Millwork Group LTD. and www.niico.com. That is the previous millwork site, not Care Bear Daycare.

nodes.label: frontend/out Pages Artifact
nodes.rationale: Node 20, Corepack, yarn or npm install, next build, then upload-pages-artifact from frontend/out and deploy-pages to the github-pages environment.

nodes.label: Test Frontend Workflow
nodes.rationale: Runs on workflow_dispatch or push to main when frontend/** or this workflow file changes. Working directory is frontend. Cancels in-progress runs in the same concurrency group.

nodes.label: Frontend Lint Job
nodes.rationale: checkout, corepack enable, setup-node with yarn cache on frontend/yarn.lock, yarn install --immutable, yarn lint.

nodes.label: Lint Job Event Guard
nodes.rationale: Lint runs only for pull_request, or for push when the ref does not contain refs/pull/. workflow_dispatch is a trigger but does not satisfy the if, so a manual run skips Lint.

nodes.label: pre-commit Hooks
nodes.rationale: pre-commit-hooks v3.4.0: trailing-whitespace, end-of-file-fixer, check-yaml, check-added-large-files, check-json.

nodes.label: pre-commit Prettier
nodes.rationale: mirrors-prettier v2.2.1 with args --config frontend/.prettierrc.

nodes.rationale: Do not bring back taupe #DBD1C0, near-black #0a0a0a, or warm brown charcoal. Do not wide-track uppercase headings, square marketing buttons, or invert the Care Bear logo. Tailwind chip hues are not brand colors.

nodes.label: contact@carebeardaycare.ca

nodes.label: Local Docker Compose Dev
nodes.rationale: docker compose up --build --remove-orphans serves http://127.0.0.1:3010. The frontend container runs yarn dev on port 3000; Caddy publishes 3010. Outside Docker: cd frontend && yarn install && yarn dev.

nodes.label: Compose Frontend Service
nodes.rationale: Builds frontend/Dockerfile.local, sets WATCHPACK_POLLING=true, and bind-mounts ./frontend to /code while keeping anonymous volumes for /code/node_modules and /code/.next.

nodes.label: Compose Caddy Reverse Proxy
nodes.rationale: reverse-proxy uses caddy:latest, depends_on frontend, publishes 3010:3010, and mounts ./Caddyfile at /etc/caddy/Caddyfile.
